text: SPECTATOR.—‘tot. Wilson's work takes rank as a history in the usual sense, and from this point of view it has a conspicuous merit, rare enough in any history of modern events, that of scrupulous impartiality, a true and impressive picture of the most marvellously rapid political evolution of which human society affords an example. . . . We may conclude this imperfect account of a fine historical work by quoting,’ etc.
ATHENÆUM.—‘Throughout the condensation is masterly. Dr. Wilson has, we think, produced the best history of the rise of the North American Republic which has yet been written.’
HARPER & BROTHERS, 45, ALBEMARLE ST., LONDON, W.
